questions.text:
किसी वैद्युत-रासायनिक सेल में निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया होती है :
2Cu+(aq) + Zn (s) → 2Cu (s) + Zn2+ (aq)
E°सेल = 1·28 V
जैसे-जैसे अभिक्रिया आगे बढ़ती है, सेल के समग्र विभव का क्या होगा ?
questions.text_english:
In an electrochemical cell, the following reaction takes place :
2Cu+(aq) + Zn (s) → 2Cu (s) + Zn2+ (aq)
E°cell = 1·28 V
As the reaction progresses, what will happen to the overall voltage of the cell ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). According to the Nernst equation, the cell voltage depends on the concentrations of reactants and products. As the reaction progresses, [Cu+] decreases (it is consumed) and [Zn2+] increases (it is produced). In the Nernst equation, [Zn2+] appears in the numerator of the reaction quotient Q. As [Zn2+] increases, Q increases, which causes the cell voltage (E = E° - (RT/nF)lnQ) to decrease. Option (C) is incorrect because [Cu+] decreases as the reaction proceeds. Option (D) is incorrect because increasing [Zn2+] actually decreases the voltage, not increases it. Option (A) is incorrect because the voltage changes as concentrations change.

questions.text:
Ti3+, Cr3+, Fe2+ और Ni2+ आयनों में से जलीय विलयन में सर्वाधिक स्थाई आयन है :
[परमाणु क्रमांक : Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.text_english:
Out of Ti3+, Cr3+, Fe2+ and Ni2+ ions, the one which is the most stable ion in aqueous solution is :
[Atomic number : Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Fe = 26, Ni = 28]
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Ni2+. Ni has atomic number 28, and its electronic configuration is [Ar] 3d8 4s2. Ni2+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d8, which is a relatively stable configuration. Ti3+ (configuration [Ar] 3d1) is easily oxidised or reduced and is not very stable. Cr3+ ([Ar] 3d3) is reasonably stable but Ni2+ is more stable in aqueous solution as it does not readily get oxidised or reduced under normal conditions. Fe2+ ([Ar] 3d6) is easily oxidised to Fe3+ in aqueous solution making it less stable. Ni2+ with a 3d8 configuration is the most stable among the given ions in aqueous solution.

questions.text: हॉफमान ब्रोमामाइड निम्नीकरण अभिक्रिया निम्नलिखित में से किसके द्वारा दी जाती है ?
questions.text_english: Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction is given by :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) R–CO–NH2. Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction involves the treatment of an amide (R–CO–NH2) with bromine in the presence of aqueous or alcoholic KOH/NaOH. The reaction results in the loss of the carbonyl carbon, producing a primary amine (R–NH2) with one fewer carbon than the original amide. The substrate must be an amide (containing the –CO–NH2 group) for this reaction to proceed. Options (A), (B), and (C) do not contain the amide group and hence cannot undergo Hoffmann bromamide degradation.

questions.text: हेनरी स्थिरांक KH का मान होता है :
questions.text_english: The value of Henry's constant KH is :

options.A: उच्चतर विलेयता वाली गैसों के लिए बृहत्तर
options.B: निम्नतर विलेयता वाली गैसों के लिए बृहत्तर
options.D: गैसों की विलेयता से संबंधित नहीं है

options_english.A: greater for gases with higher solubility
options_english.B: greater for gases with lower solubility
options_english.D: not related to the solubility of gases

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). According to Henry's law, the partial pressure of a gas above a solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution: p = KH × x. This means that KH = p/x. A gas with lower solubility will have a smaller mole fraction (x) dissolved for a given partial pressure, making KH = p/x larger. Conversely, a highly soluble gas dissolves more readily, giving a larger x for the same pressure, and thus a smaller KH. Therefore, KH is greater for gases with lower solubility. Options (C) and (D) are incorrect because KH varies from gas to gas and is inversely related to solubility.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कार्बोहाइड्रेट की हॉवर्थ संरचना में विभिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं को संख्यांकित किया गया है। एनोमरी कार्बन को किस संख्या से संख्यांकित किया गया है?
questions.text_english: In the Haworth structure of the following carbohydrate, various carbon atoms have been numbered. The anomeric carbon is numbered as :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1. The anomeric carbon is the carbon that was the carbonyl carbon (aldehyde carbon in aldoses or ketone carbon in ketoses) in the open-chain form of the sugar. In the Haworth structure of glucose (a pyranose ring), C1 is the anomeric carbon. It is the carbon that is bonded to two oxygen atoms — one as part of the ring oxygen and one as the hydroxyl group. The position of the –OH group on C1 determines the alpha (α) or beta (β) configuration of the anomer. Options (B), (C), and (D) are ordinary hydroxyl-bearing carbons and are not the anomeric carbon.
questions.topic: Carbohydrates – Haworth Structure and Anomeric Carbon

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कथनों में से सही कथन है :
questions.text_english: Out of the following statements, the correct statement is :

options.A: La वास्तव में संक्रमण श्रेणी का तत्त्व नहीं है।
options.B: Zr और Hf की परमाण्विक त्रिज्याएँ लगभग समान होती हैं।
options.D: La3+ से Lu3+ तक आयनिक त्रिज्या बढ़ती है।

options_english.A: La is actually not an element of transition series.
options_english.B: Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii.
options_english.D: Ionic radius increases from La3+ to Lu3+.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Zr (Period 5) and Hf (Period 6) have almost identical atomic radii due to the lanthanoid contraction. The filling of 4f orbitals in lanthanoids causes a significant decrease in atomic and ionic radii, so that the Period 6 transition metals (including Hf) have nearly the same radii as their Period 5 counterparts. Option (A) is incorrect because La (lanthanum) does belong to the transition series (d-block, Period 6). Option (C) is incorrect — lanthanoids are not radioactive; it is the actinoids that are radioactive. Option (D) is incorrect because ionic radius actually decreases from La3+ to Lu3+, a phenomenon known as lanthanoid contraction.

questions.text: नीचे दी गई अभिक्रिया अनुक्रम में, Y की संरचना होगी :
questions.text_english: In the given reaction sequence, the structure of Y would be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Benzene. Aniline reacts with NaNO2 and HCl at 0–5°C to form benzenediazonium chloride (X). When the diazonium salt (X) is treated with ethanol (C2H5OH), it undergoes a reduction reaction in which the diazonium group (–N2+) is replaced by a hydrogen atom through a free radical mechanism, yielding benzene. Ethanol acts as a mild reducing agent in this reaction. This reaction is an example of the Sandmeyer-type replacement, specifically the reduction of a diazonium salt. Options (A), (C), and (D) would result from different reactions of the diazonium salt.

questions.text: 2-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन, 1-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन, 2-ब्रोमोप्रोपेन और 1-ब्रोमोप्रोपेन में से कौन-सा अणु किरेल प्रकृति का है ?
questions.text_english: Out of 2-Bromobutane, 1-Bromobutane, 2-Bromopropane and 1-Bromopropane, the molecule which is chiral in nature is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 2-Bromobutane. A molecule is chiral if it contains an asymmetric (chiral) carbon atom — a carbon bonded to four different groups. In 2-bromobutane (CH3–CHBr–CH2–CH3), C2 is bonded to Br, H, CH3, and C2H5 — four different groups — making it a chiral centre. In 2-bromopropane (CH3–CHBr–CH3), C2 is bonded to Br, H, CH3, and CH3 — two identical methyl groups — so it is not chiral. 1-Bromobutane and 1-bromopropane have the Br on a terminal carbon with two hydrogens and are not chiral. Therefore, only 2-bromobutane is chiral.

questions.text: संक्रमण धातुओं के निम्नलिखित गुणधर्मों में से कौन-सा उन्हें उत्प्रेरक की भाँति व्यवहार करने योग्य बनाता है ?
questions.text_english: Which of the following properties of transition metals enables them to behave as catalysts ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Variable oxidation states. Transition metals can exist in multiple oxidation states due to the availability of closely spaced d orbitals and ns orbitals for bond formation. This ability to change oxidation states enables them to accept and donate electrons during a chemical reaction, thereby acting as effective catalysts. For example, Fe can exist as Fe2+ and Fe3+, and it catalyses the Haber process. High melting point relates to the strong metallic bonding but not catalytic activity. High ionisation enthalpy would actually make it harder to participate in reactions. Alloy formation is a property but not the reason for catalytic behaviour.

questions.text: FeO के 1 मोल को Fe2O3 में ऑक्सीकृत करने के लिए कितने विद्युत आवेश की आवश्यकता होती है ?
questions.text_english: What amount of electric charge is required for the oxidation of 1 mole of FeO to Fe2O3 ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1F. In FeO, iron is in the +2 oxidation state. In Fe2O3, iron is in the +3 oxidation state. The oxidation half-reaction is: Fe2+ → Fe3+ + e–. To convert 1 mole of FeO (containing 1 mole of Fe2+) to Fe2O3, each Fe2+ loses 1 electron to become Fe3+. Therefore, 1 mole of electrons (= 1 Faraday = 1F) of charge is required for the oxidation of 1 mole of FeO to produce Fe2O3.

questions.text: ऐल्कोहॉलों को सांद्र H2SO4 के साथ गर्म करने पर ऐल्कीन बनती हैं। अभिक्रिया का प्रथम चरण है :
questions.text_english: Alkenes are formed by heating alcohols with conc. H2SO4. The first step in the reaction is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) protonation of alcohol molecule. The dehydration of alcohols with concentrated H2SO4 follows an E1 mechanism for secondary and tertiary alcohols. The very first step is the protonation of the –OH group of the alcohol by the strong acid H2SO4, converting it into a good leaving group (water). In the second step, the protonated alcohol loses water to form a carbocation. In the third step, a proton is removed to give the alkene. So protonation precedes carbocation formation, making option (C) the correct first step. Option (A) is the second step, not the first.

questions.text: पॉलिहैलोजन यौगिकों का उद्योगों और कृषि में व्यापक अनुप्रयोग है। DDT भी एक अत्यंत महत्त्वपूर्ण पॉलिहैलोजन यौगिक है। यह है एक :
questions.text_english: Polyhalogen compounds have wide application in industries and agriculture. DDT is also a very important polyhalogen compound. It is a :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) non-biodegradable insecticide. DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is a polyhalogen compound that was widely used as an insecticide, particularly against mosquitoes and agricultural pests. It is non-biodegradable, meaning it cannot be broken down by microorganisms and persists in the environment for very long periods. This has led to its bioaccumulation in the food chain. Due to its toxic and persistent nature, DDT has been banned in many countries. It is not a greenhouse gas, fertilizer, or biodegradable insecticide.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ऐनिलीन की तुलना में ऐसीटेनिलाइड कम क्षारकीय है।
कारण (R) : ऐनिलीन के ऐसीटिलीकरण के परिणामस्वरूप नाइट्रोजन पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व घटता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Acetanilide is less basic than aniline.
Reason (R) : Acetylation of aniline results in decrease of electron density on nitrogen.
questions.instruction_line: दोनों कथनों को पढ़कर सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read both statements and select the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and the Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. In aniline, the lone pair on nitrogen is available for donation, making it basic. When aniline undergoes acetylation to form acetanilide, the lone pair of nitrogen gets delocalized into the carbonyl (C=O) group of the acetyl group through resonance. This reduces the electron density on nitrogen, making the lone pair less available for protonation. As a result, acetanilide is less basic than aniline. Thus Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

अभिकथन (A) : क्यूप्रस लवण प्रतिचुम्बकीय होते हैं।
कारण (R) : क्यूप्रस आयन में पूर्ण भरित 3d-कक्षक होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Cuprous salts are diamagnetic.
Reason (R) : Cuprous ion has completely filled 3d-orbitals.

questions.instruction_line_english: Read both statements and select the correct option.

options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. Copper (Cu) has atomic number 29 with the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d10 4s1. The cuprous ion (Cu+) is formed by loss of the 4s electron, giving the configuration [Ar] 3d10. Since all 3d orbitals are completely filled with paired electrons, there are no unpaired electrons in Cu+. A substance with no unpaired electrons is diamagnetic. Therefore, cuprous salts are diamagnetic, and the completely filled 3d10 configuration of Cu+ is the correct reason for this property.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : n-ब्यूटिल ब्रोमाइड की तुलना में n-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड का क्वथनांक उच्चतर होता है।
कारण (R) : C – Br आबंध की तुलना में C – Cl आबंध अधिक ध्रुवीय होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : n-Butyl chloride has higher boiling point than n-Butyl bromide.
Reason (R) : C – Cl bond is more polar than C – Br bond.
questions.instruction_line: दोनों कथनों को पढ़कर सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read both statements and select the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Assertion is false but the Reason is true. n-Butyl bromide actually has a higher boiling point than n-Butyl chloride, not the other way around. This is because Br is a larger atom than Cl, and bromine has more electrons, leading to stronger London dispersion (van der Waals) forces between n-butyl bromide molecules. Greater molecular mass and polarizability of Br cause stronger intermolecular forces and hence higher boiling point for n-butyl bromide. The Reason (R) is indeed true — C–Cl bond is more polar than C–Br bond because Cl is more electronegative than Br. However, boiling point in alkyl halides depends more on molecular size and van der Waals forces than on bond polarity, so the Reason does not correctly explain the (false) Assertion.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जलीय NaCl का वैद्युत-अपघटन कैथोड पर H2 और ऐनोड पर Cl2 देता है।
कारण (R) : H2O की अपेक्षा क्लोरीन का ऑक्सीकरण विभव उच्चतर होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Electrolysis of aqueous NaCl gives H2 at cathode and Cl2 at anode.
Reason (R) : Chlorine has higher oxidation potential than H2O.
questions.instruction_line: दोनों कथनों को पढ़कर सही विकल्प चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Read both statements and select the correct option.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Both the Assertion and Reason are true and Reason correctly explains the Assertion. During electrolysis of aqueous NaCl, at the cathode, H2O molecules are reduced in preference to Na+ ions (since Na+ has a very negative reduction potential), producing H2 gas. At the anode, Cl– ions are oxidised in preference to H2O molecules because Cl– has a higher oxidation potential (lower reduction potential) than H2O, meaning it is easier to oxidise Cl– than water. This is why Cl2 is liberated at the anode instead of O2. Therefore, H2 is produced at the cathode and Cl2 at the anode, and the higher oxidation potential of Cl– compared to H2O correctly explains the observation.

questions.text: आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्लों से क्या अभिप्राय है ? ऐमीनो अम्ल उभयधर्मी प्रकृति के क्यों होते हैं?
questions.text_english: What is meant by essential amino acids ? Why are amino acids amphoteric in nature ?

key_points: Essential amino acids are those that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained through diet.
Amino acids are amphoteric because they contain both an acidic group (–COOH) and a basic group (–NH2) in the same molecule.

questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body in adequate quantities and must therefore be supplied through the diet. Examples include valine, leucine, lysine, and threonine. Amino acids are amphoteric in nature because each amino acid molecule contains both an acidic carboxyl group (–COOH) and a basic amino group (–NH2). In aqueous solution, the –COOH group can donate a proton (acting as an acid) while the –NH2 group can accept a proton (acting as a base). They can thus react with both acids and bases, and in neutral solution, they exist predominantly as zwitterions (dipolar ions).

sub_questions.solution: NaBH4 is a mild and selective reducing agent. It reduces only aldehyde and ketone carbonyl groups (C=O) to the corresponding alcohols but does not reduce ester groups. In this molecule, the ketone C=O of the cyclohexanone ring is reduced to –CHOH, giving a cyclohexanol ring. The ester group (–C(=O)–OCH3) at the end of the side chain remains unreacted. The main product is methyl 3-(1-hydroxycyclohexyl)propanoate.

key_points: Tertiary alcohols react with aluminium metal to form aluminium alkoxide.

questions.text: उस सेल का नाम और परिभाषा लिखिए जिसे अपोलो अंतरिक्ष कार्यक्रम में विद्युत ऊर्जा प्रदान करने के लिए प्रयोग में लाया गया था। इसका एक लाभ भी लिखिए।
questions.text_english: Name and define the cell which was used for providing electric power in the Apollo space programme. Also write its one advantage.

key_points: The cell used was the Hydrogen-Oxygen Fuel Cell.
A fuel cell is an electrochemical cell that converts chemical energy of a fuel directly and continuously into electrical energy as long as the fuel is supplied.
One advantage: The only by-product is water, making it environmentally clean / it has high efficiency compared to thermal power plants.

questions.solution: The cell used in the Apollo space programme was the Hydrogen-Oxygen Fuel Cell. A fuel cell is a type of electrochemical cell in which the chemical energy of a fuel (hydrogen) and an oxidant (oxygen) is converted directly into electrical energy through electrochemical reactions, as long as the fuel and oxidant are continuously supplied. In this cell, hydrogen is oxidised at the anode and oxygen is reduced at the cathode, producing water as the only by-product. One major advantage of this cell is that it is environmentally friendly because it produces no pollutants — the only by-product is pure water, which was also used as drinking water by astronauts.

questions.text: PdCl2·2KCl, AgNO3 विलयन के साथ AgCl का अवक्षेप नहीं देता है। संकुल का संरचनात्मक सूत्र और IUPAC नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english: PdCl2·2KCl does not give precipitate of AgCl with AgNO3 solution. Write the structural formula and IUPAC name of the complex.

key_points: Since no AgCl precipitate forms, Cl– ions are not free in solution — all Cl– ions are coordinated to Pd.
Structural formula: K2[PdCl4]
IUPAC name: Potassium tetrachloropalladate(II)

questions.solution: Since PdCl2·2KCl does not give a precipitate with AgNO3 solution, it means that no free Cl– ions are present in solution. This indicates that all the chloride ions are present inside the coordination sphere, bonded directly to the metal. The formula of the complex is K2[PdCl4], where Pd2+ is the central metal ion coordinated to four Cl– ligands, and K+ ions are the counter ions outside the coordination sphere. The structural formula is K2[PdCl4]. Its IUPAC name is Potassium tetrachloropalladate(II).

sub_questions.text: A2(g) और B2(g) के बीच अभिक्रिया एक बन्द समतापी पात्र में की गई। अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग नियम पाया गया : वेग = k[A2][B2]। ताप को स्थिर रखते हुए यदि अभिक्रिया कोष्ठ में 1 मोल A2(g) मिलाई गई, तो अभिक्रिया वेग तथा वेग स्थिरांक में परिवर्तन की प्रागुक्ति कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: The reaction between A2(g) and B2(g) was carried out in a sealed isothermal container. The rate law for the reaction was found to be: Rate = k[A2][B2]. If 1 mole of A2(g) was added to the reaction chamber and the temperature was kept constant, then predict the change in rate of the reaction and the rate constant.

key_points: When 1 mole of A2 is added at constant temperature, [A2] increases.
Since Rate = k[A2][B2], with increased [A2], the rate of reaction will increase.
The rate constant k does not change because it depends only on temperature, which is kept constant.

sub_questions.solution: When 1 mole of A2(g) is added to the sealed isothermal container at constant temperature, the concentration of A2 increases. Since the rate law is Rate = k[A2][B2], the rate of reaction depends on the concentrations of both A2 and B2. As [A2] increases while [B2] remains the same, the rate of the reaction will increase. However, the rate constant k is temperature-dependent and does not depend on concentration. Since the temperature is kept constant, the rate constant k remains unchanged.

A constant half-life is the characteristic of a first-order reaction.
Rate law: Rate = k[A]

A constant half-life is the characteristic feature of a first-order reaction. Therefore, the reaction is of first order. questions.text:
निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक प्रेक्षण के लिए स्पष्टीकरण दीजिए :
(क) Mn3+ आयन ऑक्सीकारक है जबकि Cr2+ आयन अपचायक है यद्यपि दोनों का d-कक्षक विन्यास (d4) एक समान है।
(ख) लैंथेनॉयड आकुंचन की तुलना में एक तत्त्व से दूसरे तत्त्व के बीच ऐक्टिनॉयड आकुंचन अधिक होता है।
(ग) H, B, C और N के साथ संक्रमण धातुएँ बहुत अधिक संख्या में अंतराकाशी यौगिक बनाती हैं।
questions.text_english:
Give explanation for each of the following observations :
(a) With the same d-orbital configuration (d4), Mn3+ ion is an oxidising agent whereas Cr2+ ion is a reducing agent.
(b) Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than that among lanthanoids.
(c) Transition metals form large number of interstitial compounds with H, B, C and N.

key_points: (a) Mn3+ (d4) tends to gain an electron to form Mn2+ (d5, half-filled stable configuration) — so it is an oxidising agent. Cr2+ (d4) tends to lose an electron to form Cr3+ (d3, half-filled t2g) — so it is a reducing agent.

(b) In actinoids, 5f orbitals are more diffuse and provide poor shielding of nuclear charge, so each successive electron addition causes a larger decrease in ionic radius compared to 4f orbitals in lanthanoids.
(c) Transition metals have a suitable atomic radius and vacant d-orbitals that allow small atoms like H, B, C, and N to fit into the interstitial voids of the metallic crystal lattice.

questions.solution:
(a) Mn3+ has a d4 configuration and acts as an oxidising agent because it tends to gain one electron to attain the stable d5 (half-filled) configuration, converting to Mn2+. Cr2+ also has a d4 configuration but acts as a reducing agent because it tends to lose one electron to attain the more stable d3 configuration (half-filled t2g in octahedral field), converting to Cr3+. Thus, the direction of electron transfer — governed by the most stable configuration attainable — determines whether the ion is an oxidising or reducing agent.

(b) In actinoids, the 5f orbitals are more diffuse and less effectively shield the nuclear charge compared to the 4f orbitals in lanthanoids. As atomic number increases across the actinoid series, the poor shielding effect of 5f electrons causes a greater attraction of outer electrons by the nucleus, leading to a larger decrease in ionic radius per element compared to lanthanoids.

(c) Transition metals have a suitable atomic radius — not too large and not too small — and also have vacant d-orbitals. The small atoms of hydrogen, boron, carbon, and nitrogen can easily be accommodated in the interstitial voids (holes) present in the close-packed crystal lattice of transition metals. These atoms are held in place by metallic and covalent interactions, resulting in a large number of interstitial compounds.
questions.topic: Properties of transition metals and f-block elements

questions.text: C8H8O आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई ऐरोमैटिक यौगिक 'A' धनात्मक 2,4-DNP परीक्षण देता है। यह सोडियम हाइपोआयोडाइट के साथ अभिक्रियित किए जाने पर यौगिक 'B' का पीला अवक्षेप देता है। यौगिक 'A' टॉलेन अथवा फेलिंग अभिकर्मक के साथ अभिक्रिया नहीं करता है; KMnO4 के साथ प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण पर यह कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल 'C' बनाता है। 'A', 'B' और 'C' की संरचनाएँ स्पष्ट कीजिए। उनके IUPAC नाम भी दीजिए।
questions.text_english: An aromatic compound 'A' with molecular formula C8H8O gives positive 2,4-DNP test. It gives yellow precipitate of compound 'B' on treatment with sodium hypoiodite. Compound 'A' does not react with Tollen's or Fehling's reagent; on drastic oxidation with KMnO4 it forms a carboxylic acid 'C'. Elucidate the structures of A, B and C. Also give their IUPAC names.

key_points: A is methyl phenyl ketone (acetophenone): C6H5–CO–CH3, IUPAC name: 1-phenylethan-1-one
B is iodoform (CHI3), IUPAC name: triiodomethane
C is benzoic acid (C6H5COOH), IUPAC name: benzenecarboxylic acid

questions.solution: Compound 'A' (C8H8O) gives a positive 2,4-DNP test, indicating the presence of a carbonyl group (C=O), so it is either an aldehyde or ketone. It does not react with Tollen's or Fehling's reagent, ruling out an aldehyde. Therefore, 'A' is a ketone. The iodoform test (positive yellow precipitate with NaOI) is given by methyl ketones (CH3CO– group). Drastic oxidation with KMnO4 gives a carboxylic acid 'C'. Since 'A' is aromatic with formula C8H8O, the compound is acetophenone (C6H5COCH3). Compound A: C6H5–CO–CH3; IUPAC name: 1-phenylethan-1-one. Compound B: The yellow precipitate from the iodoform test is iodoform (CHI3); IUPAC name: triiodomethane. Compound C: Drastic KMnO4 oxidation of acetophenone gives benzoic acid (C6H5COOH); IUPAC name: benzenecarboxylic acid.

questions.text:
पूछे गए अनुसार निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को व्यवस्थित कीजिए :
(क) C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5NHCH3, C6H5NH2 — pKb मानों के घटते हुए क्रम में
(ख) C2H5OH, C2H5NH2, (CH3)2NH — क्वथनांक के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में
(ग) C6H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2 — जल में विलेयता के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following compounds as asked :
(a) in decreasing order of pKb values: C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5NHCH3, C6H5NH2
(b) increasing order of boiling point: C2H5OH, C2H5NH2, (CH3)2NH
(c) increasing order of solubility in water: C6H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2

key_points: (a) Decreasing pKb (i.e., increasing basicity order reversed): C6H5NH2 > C6H5NHCH3 > C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)2NH
(b) Increasing boiling point: (CH3)2NH < C2H5NH2 < C2H5OH
(c) Increasing solubility: C6H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH < C2H5NH2

questions.solution:
(a) Higher pKb means weaker base. Aniline (C6H5NH2) is the weakest base because the lone pair on N is delocalised into the aromatic ring. N-methylaniline (C6H5NHCH3) is slightly more basic due to the +I effect of CH3, but still weak due to ring delocalization. Among aliphatic amines, diethylamine is more basic than ethylamine due to greater +I effect. Decreasing pKb order: C6H5NH2 > C6H5NHCH3 > C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)2NH.

(b) Boiling points depend on intermolecular forces. Ethanol (C2H5OH) has the highest boiling point due to stronger O–H...O hydrogen bonding. Ethylamine (C2H5NH2) has N–H...N hydrogen bonds, which are weaker than O–H bonds, giving it a lower but still significant boiling point. Dimethylamine ((CH3)2NH) is a secondary amine with only one N–H, forming fewer and weaker hydrogen bonds, giving the lowest boiling point. Increasing boiling point order: (CH3)2NH < C2H5NH2 < C2H5OH.

(c) Solubility in water depends on hydrogen bonding with water and molecular size/hydrophobicity. C2H5NH2 (primary amine, small) is most soluble. (C2H5)2NH (secondary amine, larger hydrophobic group) is less soluble. Aniline (C6H5NH2) has poor water solubility because the large non-polar benzene ring dominates. Increasing solubility order: C6H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH < C2H5NH2.
questions.topic: Physical properties and basicity of amines

sub_questions.text: निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (i) n-प्रोपिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में ऐलिल क्लोराइड अधिक तीव्रता से जल-अपघटित होता है। (ii) ऐल्किल हैलाइडों को जब सिल्वर सायनाइड के साथ अभिक्रियित किया जाता है तब आइसोसायनाइड बनते हैं। (iii) SN2 अभिक्रिया में t-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में मेथिल क्लोराइड OH– आयन के साथ अधिक शीघ्रता से अभिक्रिया करता है।
sub_questions.text_english: Account for the following : (i) Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride. (ii) Isocyanides are formed when alkyl halides are treated with silver cyanide. (iii) Methyl chloride reacts faster with OH– ion in SN2 reaction than t-butyl chloride.

key_points: (i) Allyl carbocation is stabilised by resonance, making it easier to form during SN1 hydrolysis.
(ii) AgCN is ionic; CN– attacks through N (ambident nucleophile), forming isocyanide (R–NC).
(iii) In SN2, methyl chloride has no steric hindrance; t-butyl chloride has three bulky methyl groups blocking the backside attack.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Allyl chloride (CH2=CH–CH2Cl) is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride because the allyl carbocation (CH2=CH–CH2+), formed as an intermediate, is stabilised by resonance — the positive charge is delocalized over two carbons through the adjacent double bond. n-Propyl chloride forms a primary carbocation with no such stabilisation. The greater stability of the allyl carbocation makes the ionisation step faster.

(ii) Silver cyanide (AgCN) is an ionic compound in which the CN– acts as an ambident nucleophile — it can bond through either C or N. In AgCN, the silver polarizes the bond such that the nitrogen end of CN– is the more reactive site. Therefore, when alkyl halides react with AgCN, the nitrogen attacks the carbon of the alkyl halide to form isocyanides (R–N≡C).

(iii) In SN2 reactions, the nucleophile (OH–) must attack from the backside of the carbon bearing the leaving group. Methyl chloride (CH3Cl) has no substituents on the carbon — there is no steric hindrance, so OH– can attack easily and the reaction is fast. t-Butyl chloride has three bulky methyl groups around the central carbon, creating severe steric hindrance that prevents backside attack by the nucleophile, making the SN2 reaction very slow.

sub_questions.text: 'A' और 'B' के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखकर निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं को पूर्ण कीजिए : (i) CH3CH=CH2 → HBr/peroxide → 'A' → aq.KOH → 'B' (ii) CH3CH2CHCH3(Cl) → alc.KOH/Δ → 'A' → HBr → 'B' (iii) 'A' → Mg → CH3CH2MgCl → H2O/H+ → 'B' (main product)
sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following reactions by writing the structural formulae of 'A' and 'B' : (i) CH3CH=CH2 with HBr/Peroxide gives 'A'; 'A' with aq. KOH gives 'B'. (ii) CH3CH2CHCH3 (with Cl at C3) with alc. KOH/Δ gives 'A'; 'A' with HBr gives 'B'. (iii) 'A' with Mg gives CH3CH2MgCl; CH3CH2MgCl with H2O/H+ gives 'B' (main product).

key_points: (i) A = CH3CH2CH2Br (1-bromopropane, anti-Markovnikov addition); B = CH3CH2CH2OH (propan-1-ol)
(ii) A = CH3CH=CHCH3 (but-2-ene); B = CH3CHBrCHCH3 (but-2-yl bromide / 2-bromobutane, Markovnikov product)
(iii) A = CH3CH2Cl (chloroethane/ethyl chloride); B = CH3CH3 (ethane)

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Propene reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxide via anti-Markovnikov addition, giving 1-bromopropane (A = CH3CH2CH2Br). Treatment of 1-bromopropane with aqueous KOH (nucleophilic substitution) gives propan-1-ol (B = CH3CH2CH2OH).

(ii) 2-Chlorobutane (CH3CH2CHClCH3) undergoes elimination with alcoholic KOH on heating, giving but-2-ene (A = CH3CH=CHCH3). Reaction of but-2-ene with HBr follows Markovnikov's rule, adding Br to the more substituted carbon, giving 2-bromobutane (B = CH3CHBrCH2CH3).

(iii) Since the Grignard reagent formed is CH3CH2MgCl (ethylmagnesium chloride), the starting material 'A' must be chloroethane (CH3CH2Cl). When ethylmagnesium chloride reacts with H2O in the presence of H+, the Grignard reagent undergoes protonolysis, giving ethane as the main product (B = CH3CH3).

sub_questions.text: क्या तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल प्रोपिल ईथर बनाने के लिए सोडियम प्रोपॉक्साइड और तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड का उपयोग किया जा सकता है?
sub_questions.text_english: Can sodium propoxide and t-butyl chloride be used for the preparation of t-butyl propyl ether? Justify and suggest appropriate starting materials.

key_points: No, sodium propoxide and t-butyl chloride cannot be used because t-butyl chloride is a tertiary alkyl halide and will undergo elimination (E2) rather than SN2 with the propoxide nucleophile.
The correct combination is sodium t-butoxide and propyl chloride (primary alkyl halide undergoes SN2 cleanly).

sub_questions.solution: No, sodium propoxide (C2H5CH2ONa) and t-butyl chloride ((CH3)3CCl) cannot be used for the Williamson synthesis of t-butyl propyl ether. t-Butyl chloride is a tertiary alkyl halide, and when a strong nucleophile/base like sodium propoxide reacts with it, the bulky tertiary substrate undergoes elimination (E2 mechanism) to give isobutylene rather than the desired ether product. In Williamson synthesis, SN2 mechanism is preferred, which requires a primary (or at most secondary) alkyl halide. To prepare t-butyl propyl ether, the correct starting materials are sodium t-butoxide ((CH3)3CONa) and propyl chloride (C3H7Cl, a primary alkyl halide). The primary alkyl halide undergoes SN2 smoothly with the alkoxide to give the desired ether.

questions.text:
NaOH का एक जलीय विलयन बनाया गया और परासरण दाब की माप से 25°C पर इसका मोलर द्रव्यमान 28 g mol–1 पाया गया। इस विलयन में NaOH का प्रतिशत वियोजन परिकलित कीजिए।
[परमाणु द्रव्यमान : Na = 23.0 u, O = 16.0 u, H = 1.0 u]
questions.text_english:
An aqueous solution of NaOH was made and its molar mass from the measurement of osmotic pressure at 25°C was found to be 28 g mol–1. Calculate the percentage dissociation of NaOH in this solution.
[Atomic mass : Na = 23.0 u, O = 16.0 u, H = 1.0 u]

key_points: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol
van't Hoff factor i = M(actual)/M(observed) = 40/28
NaOH dissociates as NaOH → Na+ + OH–; if α is degree of dissociation, i = 1 + α

questions.solution: The actual molar mass of NaOH = 23.0 + 16.0 + 1.0 = 40 g mol–1. The observed molar mass from osmotic pressure measurement = 28 g mol–1. The van't Hoff factor i = M(actual)/M(observed) = 40/28 = 10/7. NaOH dissociates as: NaOH ⇌ Na+ + OH–. If the degree of dissociation is α, then for 1 mole of NaOH, the total number of moles after dissociation = (1 – α) + α + α = 1 + α. Therefore, i = 1 + α. So 1 + α = 10/7, giving α = 10/7 – 1 = 3/7 ≈ 0.4286. Percentage dissociation of NaOH = (3/7) × 100 ≈ 42.86%.
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure and van't Hoff factor

questions.text:
25°C पर निम्नलिखित अर्ध-सेलों को जोड़कर बने वोल्टीय सेल का सेल विभव परिकलित कीजिए :

Calculate the cell voltage of the voltaic cell which is set up by joining the following half-cells at 25°C.
Al/Al3+ (0·002 M) and Ni/Ni2+ (0·002 M)
Given : E°Ni2+/Ni = –0·25 V, E°Al3+/Al = –1·66 V, log 5 = 0·6990

key_points: Cell: Al | Al3+ (0.002 M) || Ni2+ (0.002 M) | Ni (Al is anode, Ni is cathode)
E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.25 – (–1.66) = 1.41 V
Overall reaction: 2Al + 3Ni2+ → 2Al3+ + 3Ni; n = 6

questions.solution: Since E°Al3+/Al (–1.66 V) < E°Ni2+/Ni (–0.25 V), Al acts as the anode (oxidation) and Ni acts as the cathode (reduction). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.25 – (–1.66) = 1.41 V. The overall cell reaction is: 2Al + 3Ni2+ → 2Al3+ + 3Ni. Number of electrons transferred n = 6. Reaction quotient Q = [Al3+]²/[Ni2+]³ = (0.002)²/(0.002)³ = 1/0.002 = 500. Using Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log Q = 1.41 – (0.0591/6) × log 500 = 1.41 – (0.00985) × log(100 × 5) = 1.41 – 0.00985 × (2 + log 5) = 1.41 – 0.00985 × (2 + 0.6990) = 1.41 – 0.00985 × 2.699 = 1.41 – 0.0266 ≈ 1.383 V.

questions.text: आदर्श विलयन की सामान्यत: स्वीकृत परिभाषा के अनुसार उसी अथवा भिन्न स्पीशीज़ के अणुओं के मध्य समान अन्योन्यक्रिया बल कार्य करते हैं। (यह कथन तुल्य है कि घटकों की सक्रियता उनकी सांद्रता के बराबर होती है।) सच पूछिए तो यह शर्त मिश्रणों (ध्रुण समावयव, तत्त्व के समस्थानिक मिश्रणों, हाइड्रोकार्बन मिश्रणों) के लिए केवल अपवादात्मक प्रकरणों में ही पूरी होती है। आदर्श विलयनों के विषय में सीमित प्रकरणों में ही चर्चा की जा सकती है क्योंकि विलायक के संदर्भ में अत्यंत तनु विलयन ही आदर्शत: व्यवहार करते हैं। इस दृष्टिकोण को इस तथ्य से और भी समर्थन मिला कि राउल्ट नियम ने तनु विलयनों में विलायक के व्यवहार का वर्णन करने के लिए आनुभविक रूप से ज्ञात किया तथा पूर्वधारणा के माध्यम से ऊष्मागतिकी द्वारा विलायक के आदर्श व्यवहार को निगमित किया जा सकता है।
questions.text_english: According to the generally accepted definition of the ideal solution there are equal interaction forces acting between molecules belonging to the same or different species. (This is equivalent to the statement that the activity of the components equals the concentration.) Strictly speaking, this condition is fulfilled only in exceptional cases for mixtures (optical isomers, isotopic mixtures of an element, hydrocarbon mixtures). It is still usual to talk about ideal solutions as limiting cases in reality since very dilute solutions behave ideally with respect to the solvent. This view is further supported by the fact that Raoult's law empirically found for describing the behaviour of the solvent in dilute solutions can be deduced thermodynamically via the assumption of ideal behaviour of the solvent.

sub_questions.text_english: Give one example of miscible liquid pair which shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. What is the reason for such deviation?

key_points: Example: Chloroform and acetone (CHCl3 and CH3COCH3)

Reason: The interaction between unlike molecules (CHCl3–CH3COCH3 through hydrogen bonding) is stronger than the interactions between like molecules, leading to lower vapour pressure than predicted by Raoult's law.

sub_questions.solution: One example of a miscible liquid pair showing negative deviation from Raoult's law is chloroform (CHCl3) and acetone (CH3COCH3). The reason for negative deviation is that the intermolecular interactions between unlike molecules (A–B type) are stronger than the interactions between like molecules (A–A or B–B type). In this case, chloroform forms hydrogen bonds with acetone, resulting in stronger A–B interactions. This causes the vapour pressure of the solution to be lower than what would be predicted by Raoult's law, hence a negative deviation.

sub_questions.text_english: State Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components.

key_points: Raoult's law: For a solution containing volatile components, the partial vapour pressure of each component is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution. p_i = x_i × p°_i

sub_questions.solution: Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components states that the partial vapour pressure of each volatile component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction present in solution. Mathematically, for component i: p_i = x_i × p°_i, where p_i is the partial vapour pressure of component i, x_i is its mole fraction in solution, and p°_i is the vapour pressure of the pure component i at the same temperature.

sub_questions.text: राउल्ट का नियम हेनरी के नियम की एक विशेष स्थिति है। टिप्पणी कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Raoult's law is a special case of Henry's law. Comment.

key_points: Henry's law: p = KH × x. Raoult's law: p = p° × x. When KH = p° (pure component vapour pressure), the two laws become identical, showing Raoult's law is a special case of Henry's law.

sub_questions.solution: Henry's law states that the partial pressure of a dissolved gas is proportional to its mole fraction in solution: p = KH × x. Raoult's law states that the partial vapour pressure of a volatile component equals the product of its mole fraction and vapour pressure of the pure component: p = p° × x. If we consider the solvent in a dilute ideal solution, it obeys Raoult's law with KH = p° (the vapour pressure of the pure solvent). Thus, Raoult's law is a special case of Henry's law where the Henry's law constant KH equals the vapour pressure of the pure component p°.

(2) The enthalpy of mixing is zero (ΔH_mix = 0) and the volume of mixing is also zero (ΔV_mix = 0), indicating no change in intermolecular forces or molecular sizes upon mixing.

questions.text: राइबोस और 2-डिऑक्सीराइबोस की जीव विज्ञान में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका है। उनके सबसे महत्त्वपूर्ण व्युत्पन्न वे हैं जिनमें फॉस्फेट समूह 5-स्थिति से बँधता है। मोनो-, डाई- और ट्राई-फॉस्फेट रूप तथा 3-5 चक्रीय मोनोफॉस्फेट महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं। प्यूरीन और पिरिमिडीन, राइबोस तथा डिऑक्सीराइबोस के साथ यौगिकों का एक मुख्य वर्ग बनाते हैं। जब ये प्यूरीन और पिरिमिडीन व्युत्पन्न राइबोस शर्करा के साथ युग्मन करते हैं, तो ये न्यूक्लियोसाइड कहलाते हैं।
questions.text_english: Ribose and 2-deoxyribose have an important role in biology. Among the most important derivatives are those with phosphate groups attached at the 5 position. Mono-, di- and tri-phosphate forms are important, as well as 3-5 cyclic monophosphates. Purines and pyrimidines form an important class of compounds with ribose and deoxyribose. When these purine and pyrimidine derivatives are coupled to a ribose sugar, they are called nucleosides.

sub_questions.text: जब DNA को जल-अपघटित किया जाता है तो क्या उत्पाद बनेंगे? संरचना के संदर्भ में DNA किस प्रकार RNA से भिन्न है?
sub_questions.text_english: What products would be formed when DNA is hydrolysed? How is DNA different from RNA with reference to a structure?

key_points: Hydrolysis of DNA gives: phosphoric acid, deoxyribose sugar, and nitrogenous bases (adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine).
DNA differs from RNA structurally in two ways: DNA contains deoxyribose sugar while RNA contains ribose sugar; DNA contains thymine as a base while RNA contains uracil instead.

sub_questions.solution: When DNA is hydrolysed completely, it produces three types of products: phosphoric acid (H3PO4), 2-deoxyribose sugar, and four nitrogenous bases — adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T). DNA differs from RNA in two structural ways: firstly, DNA contains 2-deoxyribose as its pentose sugar, whereas RNA contains ribose (which has an –OH group at the 2' carbon instead of –H); secondly, the pyrimidine base thymine (5-methyluracil) is present in DNA but absent in RNA, which instead contains uracil.

sub_questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइड और न्यूक्लियोसाइड में अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Differentiate between nucleotide and nucleoside.

key_points: Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar (no phosphate).
Nucleotide = nitrogenous base + pentose sugar + phosphate group.

sub_questions.solution: A nucleoside is formed by the combination of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) and a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) through an N-glycosidic bond. It does not contain a phosphate group. A nucleotide, on the other hand, is a nucleoside that has a phosphate group attached to the 5'-carbon of the sugar. In other words, nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group. Nucleotides are the monomeric units of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).

sub_questions.text: न्यूक्लीक अम्ल के दो महत्त्वपूर्ण प्रकार्यों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Mention two important functions of nucleic acid.

key_points: 1. DNA stores and transmits genetic information from one generation to the next (heredity).
2. RNA is responsible for protein synthesis by directing the assembly of amino acids (via transcription and translation).

sub_questions.solution: Two important functions of nucleic acids are: (1) DNA stores genetic information in the sequence of its bases and transmits this hereditary information from parent to offspring during cell division. (2) RNA (mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA) plays a central role in protein synthesis by carrying the genetic message from DNA to the ribosomes, where it directs the synthesis of proteins.

key_points: The linkage joining two nucleotides is the 3',5'-phosphodiester bond.
The base found in RNA but not in DNA is Uracil.

sub_questions.solution: Two nucleotides in a nucleic acid chain are joined by a 3',5'-phosphodiester bond, formed between the phosphate group attached to the 5' carbon of one nucleotide and the 3'-OH group of the adjacent nucleotide sugar. sub_questions.text: (i) कारण दीजिए : (I) [Ni(CO)4] प्रतिचुम्बकीय है जबकि [NiCl4]2– अनुचुम्बकीय है। [परमाणु क्रमांक Ni = 28] (II) NH3 की तुलना में CO एक प्रबल संकुलन कर्मक है। (III) संकुल [Co(en)2Cl2]+ का विपक्ष समावयव ध्रुवण अघूर्णक है। (ii) क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत का उपयोग करते हुए Fe3+ के अष्टफलकीय संकुलों में निम्नलिखित की उपस्थिति में अयुगलित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या लिखिए : (I) प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगन्ड (II) दुर्बल क्षेत्र लिगन्ड [परमाणु क्रमांक Fe = 26]
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Give reasons : (I) [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic whereas [NiCl4]2– is paramagnetic. (II) CO is a stronger complexing agent than NH3. (III) The trans isomer of complex [Co(en)2Cl2]+ is optically inactive. (ii) Using Crystal Field theory, write the number of unpaired electrons in octahedral complexes of Fe3+ in presence of: (I) Strong field ligand (II) Weak field ligand [Atomic number Fe = 26]

key_points: (I) In [Ni(CO)4], CO is a strong field ligand causing pairing: Ni is Ni(0) with 3d10 4s0 — all electrons paired, so diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]2–, Ni2+ has 3d8 config; Cl– is weak field, so electrons remain unpaired (sp3 hybridisation), giving 2 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic.
(II) CO is a stronger ligand because it acts as both a sigma donor and a pi acceptor (back bonding from metal d to CO pi*), while NH3 is only a sigma donor.
(III) Trans-[Co(en)2Cl2]+ has a plane of symmetry and centre of symmetry making it superimposable on its mirror image — hence optically inactive.
(ii)(I) With strong field ligand: Fe3+ has d5; pairing occurs, all 5 electrons pair into t2g giving 1 unpaired electron.
(ii)(II) With weak field ligand: Fe3+ has d5; electrons remain in high-spin configuration — t2g3 eg2 — giving 5 unpaired electrons.

sub_questions.solution:
(i)(I) In [Ni(CO)4], nickel is in zero oxidation state with the electronic configuration 3d10 4s0. CO is a strong field ligand, and in Ni(0), all 10 d-electrons are paired. Since there are no unpaired electrons, the complex is diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]2–, nickel is in the +2 oxidation state with 3d8 configuration. Cl– is a weak field ligand and does not cause pairing; the complex adopts sp3 hybridisation with 2 unpaired electrons, making it paramagnetic.

(i)(II) CO is a stronger complexing agent than NH3 because CO acts not only as a sigma donor (donating a lone pair to the metal) but also as a pi acceptor through back bonding, in which filled metal d-orbitals overlap with the empty pi* (antibonding) orbitals of CO. This synergistic bonding significantly strengthens the metal-ligand bond. NH3 is only a sigma donor with no pi accepting ability.

(i)(III) The trans isomer of [Co(en)2Cl2]+ has the two Cl– ligands on opposite sides of the cobalt centre. This arrangement gives the molecule a plane of symmetry (the plane containing Co, the two Cl atoms, and the midpoints of the en ligands) and a centre of inversion. Because the molecule is superimposable on its mirror image, it is achiral and hence optically inactive.

(ii) Fe has atomic number 26 with electronic configuration [Ar] 3d6 4s2. Fe3+ has the configuration [Ar] 3d5. (I) In the presence of a strong field ligand in an octahedral complex, the crystal field splitting energy Δo is large, forcing all 5 electrons to pair in the lower energy t2g orbitals. Configuration: t2g5 eg0, giving 1 unpaired electron. (II) In the presence of a weak field ligand, Δo is small, electrons remain unpaired (high spin). Configuration: t2g3 eg2, giving 5 unpaired electrons.

sub_questions.text: (i) निम्नलिखित यौगिकों द्वारा प्रदर्शित समावयविता के प्रकार का नाम लिखिए। उनके संगत समावयवों का चित्र भी बनाइए। (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] (II) [Co(en)3]3+ (III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] (ii) दुर्बल क्षेत्र और प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगन्डों के बीच अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए। लिगन्ड की प्रबलता किस प्रकार संकुल के प्रचक्रण को प्रभावित करती है?
sub_questions.text_english: (i) Name the type of isomerism exhibited by the following compounds. Also draw their corresponding isomers. (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] (II) [Co(en)3]3+ (III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] (ii) Differentiate between weak field and strong field ligands. How does the strength of the ligand influence the spin of the complex?

key_points: (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows Ionisation isomerism: isomer is [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6]
(II) [Co(en)3]3+ shows Optical isomerism: d (Δ) and l (Λ) enantiomers
(III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] shows Facial (fac) and Meridional (mer) geometrical isomerism
(ii) Weak field ligands cause small Δo (high-spin complex, more unpaired electrons); strong field ligands cause large Δo (low-spin complex, electrons pair up).

sub_questions.solution:
(i)(I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] exhibits ionisation isomerism. The isomer is [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6], where the metal ions in the cationic and anionic complexes are exchanged.

(i)(II) [Co(en)3]3+ exhibits optical isomerism. Since en (ethylenediamine) is a bidentate ligand, the tris(en) complex has no plane of symmetry and exists as non-superimposable mirror images — the d (Δ, right-handed) and l (Λ, left-handed) enantiomers.

(i)(III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] exhibits geometrical isomerism — specifically fac (facial) and mer (meridional) isomerism. In the fac isomer, the three NO2 groups occupy the three corners of one face of the octahedron. In the mer isomer, the three NO2 groups are arranged in a plane that includes the central metal.

(ii) Weak field ligands (e.g., F–, Cl–, Br–, I–, H2O) produce a small crystal field splitting energy (Δo). This means the energy required to pair electrons is greater than Δo, so electrons remain unpaired and occupy the eg orbitals — resulting in a high-spin complex with more unpaired electrons. Strong field ligands (e.g., CN–, CO, en) produce a large Δo, so it is energetically favourable for electrons to pair up in the lower t2g orbitals — resulting in a low-spin complex with fewer unpaired electrons. Therefore, the strength of the ligand directly determines the spin state of the complex: strong field → low spin; weak field → high spin.

sub_questions.text: (i) प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया N2O5(g) → 2NO2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) के लिए N2O5 की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता 1·2×10–2 mol L–1 थी। 60 मिनट के पश्चात N2O5 की सांद्रता 0·2×10–2 mol L–1 थी। 318 K पर अभिक्रिया का वेग स्थिरांक परिकलित कीजिए। [log 6 = 0·778] (ii) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए: (I) हम संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण के आधार पर किसी अभिक्रिया की कोटि ज्ञात नहीं कर सकते। (II) कोई द्वि-अणुक अभिक्रिया विशिष्ट परिस्थिति में गतिकत: प्रथम कोटि की हो सकती है।
sub_questions.text_english: (i) The initial concentration of N2O5 in the first order reaction: N2O5(g) → 2NO2(g) + 1/2 O2(g) was 1·2×10–2 mol L–1. The concentration of N2O5 after 60 minutes was 0·2×10–2 mol L–1. Calculate the rate constant at 318 K. [log 6 = 0·778] (ii) Account for the following: (I) We cannot determine the order of a reaction by taking into consideration the balanced chemical equation. (II) A bimolecular reaction may become kinetically of first order under a specified condition.

key_points: (ii)(I) Order is an experimentally determined quantity; it depends on the actual mechanism, not the stoichiometry.
(ii)(II) In a pseudo-first order reaction, when one reactant is in large excess, its concentration remains essentially constant, so the rate appears to depend only on the other reactant.

sub_questions.solution:
(i) For a first-order reaction, k = (2.303/t) × log([A]0/[A]t). Here t = 60 min, [A]0 = 1.2 × 10–2 mol L–1, [A]t = 0.2 × 10–2 mol L–1. k = (2.303/60) × log(1.2/0.2) = (2.303/60) × log 6 = (2.303/60) × 0.778 = (1.792/60) = 0.02986 min–1 ≈ 2.98 × 10–2 min–1.

(ii)(I) The order of a reaction cannot be determined from the balanced chemical equation because the rate law is determined experimentally. The stoichiometry of the reaction gives the molecularity (number of molecules involved in the elementary step), but the actual rate law depends on the mechanism, which may involve multiple steps. A reaction may have a complex mechanism with slow and fast steps, and only the rate-determining (slowest) step governs the rate law.

(ii)(II) A bimolecular reaction involving two different reactants A and B with the rate law: Rate = k[A][B] can become pseudo-first order when one of the reactants (say B) is present in a very large excess. Under this condition, the concentration of B remains essentially constant throughout the reaction, and the rate appears to depend only on [A]: Rate = k'[A], where k' = k[B] is the pseudo-first-order rate constant. For example, the acid hydrolysis of an ester in excess water follows pseudo-first-order kinetics.

(ii)(2) Overall order = 2 (first order in H2O2 and first order in I–); molecularity of the rate-determining step = 2 (bimolecular)

sub_questions.solution:
(i) Using the Arrhenius equation in logarithmic form: log(k2/k1) = Ea(T2–T1) / (2.303R × T1 × T2). Given: k2/k1 = 2, T1 = 298 K, T2 = 308 K, log 2 = 0.3, 2.303R = 19.15 JK–1mol–1. Ea = [log(k2/k1) × 2.303R × T1 × T2] / (T2–T1) = [0.3 × 19.15 × 298 × 308] / 10 = [0.3 × 19.15 × 91784] / 10 = [527,729.46 × 0.3] / 10 = 158,319 / 10 = 52,758 J mol–1 ≈ 52.76 kJ mol–1.

(ii)(1) The rate law is determined by the slowest (rate-determining) step. Step (I) is: H2O2 + I– → H2O + IO– (slow). Therefore, the rate law is: Rate = k[H2O2][I–].

(ii)(2) The overall order of the reaction is 2 (first order with respect to H2O2 and first order with respect to I–, giving a total order of 1 + 1 = 2). The molecularity of the rate-determining step (step I) is 2, as two molecular species (H2O2 and I–) are involved in the slow elementary step.

sub_questions.text_english: (i) Complete the following reactions by writing the structure of the main products: (I) Cyclohexanone + H2NCONH-NH2 → (semicarbazide) (II) (CH3)2Cd + 2CH3COCl → (III) Benzoyl chloride + H2/Pd-BaSO4 →. (ii) Give simple chemical test to distinguish between the following pairs: (I) Ethyl benzoate and benzoic acid (II) Propanal and propanone

key_points: (I) Product: Cyclohexanone semicarbazone (cyclic ring with =N-NH-CO-NH2 substituent)
(II) Product: 2CH3COCH3 (acetone/propanone) + CdCl2
(III) Product: Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) — Rosenmund reduction
(ii)(I) Benzoic acid turns blue litmus red / gives brisk effervescence with Na2CO3; ethyl benzoate does neither.
(ii)(II) Propanal gives silver mirror with Tollen's reagent / red precipitate with Fehling's solution; propanone does not.

sub_questions.solution:
(i)(I) Cyclohexanone reacts with semicarbazide (H2NCONH-NH2) through a nucleophilic addition-elimination reaction to form cyclohexanone semicarbazone. The product has the structure: cyclohexane ring with =N-NH-CONH2 group at the carbonyl position.

(i)(II) Dimethylcadmium (CH3)2Cd reacts with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in a nucleophilic acyl substitution reaction. Cadmium compounds react with acid chlorides to give ketones. The product is: 2CH3COCH3 (acetone) + CdCl2.

(i)(III) Benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl) is reduced with H2 over Pd-BaSO4 catalyst (Rosenmund reduction). The palladium catalyst is poisoned by BaSO4, which prevents over-reduction to the alcohol. The product is benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO).

(ii)(I) To distinguish ethyl benzoate from benzoic acid: add sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) solution. Benzoic acid reacts with Na2CO3 to give brisk effervescence (CO2 gas released) as it is acidic. Ethyl benzoate is a neutral ester and does not react with Na2CO3 — no effervescence is observed.

(ii)(II) To distinguish propanal from propanone: add Tollen's reagent ([Ag(NH3)2]+). Propanal (an aldehyde) reduces Tollen's reagent to give a silver mirror on the test tube wall. Propanone (a ketone) does not reduce Tollen's reagent and no silver mirror is formed.

(II) Cyclohexylidene (=CH2) with ? gives cyclohexane-CHO (III) 4-oxocyclohexane-1-carbaldehyde + [Ag(NH3)2]+ → ? (ii) Carry out the following conversions: (I) Benzaldehyde to Benzophenone (II) Benzaldehyde to 3-phenyl propanol

key_points: (I) Ethylbenzene oxidised by KMnO4/KOH then H3O+ gives benzoic acid (C6H5COOH)
(II) Reagent is O3 followed by Zn/H2O (ozonolysis) to convert =CH2 to -CHO
(III) The aldehyde group is oxidised by Tollen's reagent to carboxylate; product is 4-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid (silver mirror also forms)
(ii)(I) Benzaldehyde + C6H5MgBr (phenylmagnesium bromide) → after hydrolysis gives diphenylmethanol → oxidise with PCC or CrO3 → benzophenone

(ii)(II) Benzaldehyde + CH2=CH2 (via aldol / Wittig) or: Benzaldehyde → reduce to benzyl alcohol → convert to PhCH2CH2CH2OH via chain extension using Grignard / or: PhCHO → NaBH4 → PhCH2OH → PBr3 → PhCH2Br → Mg/ether → Grignard + HCHO → PhCH2CH2OH (not 3-phenyl); alternatively PhCHO + CH3CHO aldol → cinnamaldehyde → reduce to 3-phenylpropan-1-ol

sub_questions.solution:
(i)(I) When ethylbenzene (C6H5CH2CH3) is treated with KMnO4/KOH followed by acidification with H3O+, the alkyl side chain is oxidised. Since the carbon attached to the ring bears a hydrogen, strong KMnO4 oxidation cleaves the side chain down to the ring, giving benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) as the product.

(i)(II) To convert cyclohexylidene (=CH2, a terminal alkene) to cyclohexane-carbaldehyde (an aldehyde), the missing reagent is ozonolysis: treat with O3 followed by reductive workup (Zn/H2O). Ozonolysis of the terminal C=CH2 double bond cleaves it to give the aldehyde –CHO on the ring carbon.

(i)(III) The compound 4-oxocyclohexane-1-carbaldehyde contains an aldehyde group (–CHO) and a ketone group (C=O in the ring). [Ag(NH3)2]+ (Tollen's reagent) selectively oxidises the aldehyde group (not the ketone). The product is 4-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid (the –CHO is oxidised to –COOH), along with a silver mirror deposit.

(ii)(I) To convert benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) to benzophenone (C6H5COC6H5): React benzaldehyde with phenylmagnesium bromide (C6H5MgBr, a Grignard reagent) in dry ether, followed by hydrolysis to give diphenylmethanol (C6H5CH(OH)C6H5). Then oxidise diphenylmethanol with an oxidising agent such as PCC (pyridinium chlorochromate) or CrO3/H2SO4 to obtain benzophenone (C6H5COC6H5).

(ii)(II) To convert benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) to 3-phenylpropan-1-ol (C6H5CH2CH2CH2OH): Step 1 — React benzaldehyde with acetaldehyde (CH3CHO) under base-catalysed aldol condensation to give cinnamaldehyde (PhCH=CHCHO). Step 2 — Reduce cinnamaldehyde completely with NaBH4 or LiAlH4 to give 3-phenylpropan-1-ol (C6H5CH2CH2CH2OH).
